title: Output fragment ordering and backfill reconciliation across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Aisha Khatri
description:
Summary:
Several customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments reported intermittent malformed or misordered structured outputs when using function/tool calling with streaming responses. Symptoms include: JSON objects split across chunks arriving out of order, truncated final tokens, and deterministic misplacement of short metadata fragments ("meta" keys) when a connection is retried or when a proxy in front of the runtime performs an early retry.

Scope & Impact:
- Affects streaming tool-call responses and long multi-segment structured payloads (typical with multi-tool workflows).
- Occurs in Hosted (customer A, B), Dedicated (customer C), and an on-prem Private deployment (customer D).
- Failure modes: (1) downstream parsers fail with parse errors; (2) applications receive coherent JSON arrays but with elements out of the originally intended order; (3) silent data loss where trailing attachments are dropped and clients only notice via downstream validation failures.

Reproduction steps (local):
1. Use the reproduce harness in /confluence/structured-output/incidents/ENG-63412 (link below) and the attached sample prompt that triggers multi-tool fan-out.
2. Enable streaming on the request and configure a short chunk threshold (e.g., 256 bytes) to force multiple send events.
3. Run the request under a simulated proxy that will deliberately drop the second TCP packet and perform a retry with earlier chunks replayed.
4. Observe in the runtime assembler logs that chunk sequence IDs collide for a tenant that also has a per-tenant KV alias configured.

Initial triage and hypothesis:
- Root cause hypothesis: an edge case in the stream-sequencer that reuses transient chunk sequence IDs when a proxy-layer retry occurs combined with a weak invariant in the backfill reconciler. When retries re-ingest already-acknowledged chunks, the assembler's ordering map treats the retry as a new fragment and appends it after the current buffer instead of reconciling with the prior sequence. The bug surface is amplified when per-tenant session aliasing causes overlapping sequence windows across logical sessions on Dedicated/Private routing paths.
- Evidence: correlating runtime logs from customer A and local harness shows same chunk_id reused within a 3s window; the assembler logs show a "late_fragment" path rather than dedup/reconcile.

Immediate mitigation performed (prod):
- 2026-03-11 03:12 UTC: Enabled a conservative de-duplication gate in the edge proxy for affected customers (customer A and C). This reduced incidents but did not fully resolve out-of-order deliveries for Private deployments behind older proxies.
- 2026-03-11 09:40 UTC: Rolled runtime patch (canary) that forces strict monotonic checks on incoming chunk sequence numbers per-session; canary on 10% of Hosted traffic for 2 hours with no regressions observed.

Planned fix (work items):
- Implement robust backfill reconciliation in the assembler: detect duplicate chunk IDs and merge with existing slot instead of appending (ENG-63412-1). (In progress)
- Add tenancy-scoped sequence namespace so sequence IDs cannot collide across alias windows (ENG-63412-2). (Planned)
- Strengthen integration tests to simulate proxy retries and TCP packet reordering across Hosted/Dedicated/Private topologies (ENG-63412-3). (Planned)
- Add a metric/alert on assembler late_fragment_rate and on dedup_merge_rate to detect regression after rollout (ENG-63412-4). (Planned)

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for assembler dedupe/merge logic with 50k randomized chunk sequences.
- Integration tests with the proxy simulator used by customers (script in GH PR).
- Staging soak in dedicated environment with per-tenant aliasing toggled on/off.

Rollback & contingency:
- Rollback path: revert monotonic-check patch and disable the proxy de-dup gate. Rollback playbook written and tested in staging.
- Customer remediation: for customers who saw data corruption, we reconstructed the last successful full-response from structured-output replay logs and issued a data backfill (customer coordination tickets created).

Related artifacts & links:
- Confluence incident writeup: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/ENG-63412+Output+fragment+ordering+incident
- GitHub PR (fix branch): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5783
- Reproduction harness & proxy simulator: https://github.com/redwood-inference/streaming-tests/tree/main/eng-63412
- Alert dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streams/assembler-latency?orgId=1&var-cluster=prod
- Customer escalation threads: slack://channel/esc-hosted-toolcall

Open questions and trade-offs:
- Strict monotonic enforcement reduces risk of reordering but may increase tail latency when clients legitimately interleave chunks from different logical sessions that reuse an ID (rare). We need to balance correctness vs latency for high-throughput tenants.
- Whether to encode a longer-lived namespace in the chunk ID (adds wire-protocol compatibility concerns with older proxies) vs tenancy-scoped sequence mapping in the runtime (local-only change). Current plan favors a runtime mapping to avoid protocol churn.

Acceptance criteria for Done:
1. No further customer reports for 7 rolling days for affected customers after rollout.
2. Assembler late_fragment_rate < 1e-5 and dedup_merge_rate > 0 for 99% of traffic in prod.
3. Integration tests covering three retry scenarios (proxy retry, TCP reorder, client reconnect) are green in CI.
4. Postmortem published in Confluence and customer-facing incident summary sent.

Notes for reviewers:
- When reviewing the PR, focus on the concurrency semantics in assembler::insert_fragment (race conditions identified at lines 214-236).
- Pay attention to memory growth in the merging path; the PR includes bounded retention and eviction unit tests.
